newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - US Sept industrial output up 0.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - US Sept industrial output up 0.2 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Federal Reserve reported U.S. industrial production rose 0.2 percent in September, following a revised 0.4-percent increase in August. Capacity utilization fell to 83.3 percent from a revised 83.4percent in August.
WALDO BEST, SENIOR ECONOMIST, BZW GOVERNMENT SECURITIES, INC: "Pretty much an as-expected number. It's not going to cause any change in market view or Fed policy. Net-net its a neutral number."

Speaking to Reuters Financial Television, Best continued: "The number was a little bit stronger due to what some people were anticipating in terms of autos they had that number down a lot more than it came in," Best said. "The manufacturing number came in a little bit stronger than expected but overall the production number was as expected."
MARILYN SCHAJA, ECONOMIST, DONALDSON, LUFKIN AND JENRETTE:
"I think that basically the industrial production came in right close to the expectations, indicating continued moderate improvement in the manufacturing sector.

"There were no real surprises in the report at all. It was a little bit stronger than what it had been anticipated with manufacturing production up 0.2 percent and capacity at 83.3 percent ... (But) it continues to be good news in terms of not indicating significant capacity constrains."
IRWIN KELLNER, CHIEF ECONOMIST AT CHASE REGIONAL BANK:
"It's a little bit stronger than the markets had expected. But still 0.2 percent is not a strong number to be sure.
"But there was a big build-up in business equipment which reflects the ongoing investment that companies are making in technology. That is a plus for the economy going forward.
"Utilities output went up somewhat more slowly; that could reflect a return to more normal weather.
"As far as markets are concerned, it's one more in a series of statistics suggesting the economy has slowed down. The bond seems to be holding its gain right now.
